action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left temporal 5.4 cm mass with thick irregular nodular ring enhancement, central necrosis, rim restricted diffusion, extensive vasogenic edema involving the optic radiation and 5 mm rightward midline shift
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the left temporal lesion, define mass effect, and plan surgical approach
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI with a standardised tumour protocol characterises the lesion and its mass effect, identifies the target for tissue sampling and is required before surgery (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: rCBV ratio 4.3 in the enhancing rim, supporting a high-grade neoplasm and identifying the target for tissue sampling; mildly raised perilesional rCBV
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess tumor vascularity and target the highest-grade region for tissue sampling
action_criteria.rationale: Elevated rCBV supports a high-grade neoplasm and points to the most vascular region to sample; tissue decides the diagnosis (Law 2003).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA ratio 13.3 with prominent lipid and lactate peaks in the enhancing component, supporting a high-grade neoplasm
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize the tumor metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: A raised Cho/NAA ratio with lipid and lactate supports a high-grade neoplasm; it does not replace tissue (Bulik 2013).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary malignancy or metastatic disease
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis if a solitary metastasis remains on the differential
action_criteria.rationale: A former smoker of 64 with a single necrotic mass can have a metastasis; body staging is optional when the imaging favours a primary glioma.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No contraindication to surgery: normal blood count, platelets, electrolytes, renal and liver tests and coagulation; type and screen completed; mildly raised ESR and CRP
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory work-up: CBC, metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT) and type and screen before neurosurgery
action_criteria.rationale: Platelets, coagulation and a type and screen must be known before a neurosurgical procedure, and baseline glucose and electrolytes on dexamethasone.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: KPS 70, ECOG 2: self-caring but unable to work because of the aphasia
action_criteria.label: Record performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: Performance status selects the treatment branch after the integrated diagnosis; KPS below 70 is the unfavourable threshold (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Language left-lateralised with Wernicke area activation 4 mm from the enhancing margin; task performance limited by the comprehension deficit
action_criteria.label: Order functional MRI for language lateralisation and mapping of Wernicke and Broca areas before surgery
action_criteria.rationale: A dominant temporal tumour reaching the temporoparietal junction in an aphasic patient; functional MRI shows how close language cortex lies and whether awake mapping is feasible (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left arcuate fasciculus partly infiltrated 2 mm from the margin; optic radiation within the FLAIR abnormality 3 mm from the margin; corticospinal tract 14 mm
action_criteria.label: Order DTI tractography of the left arcuate fasciculus and optic radiation before surgery
action_criteria.rationale: The FLAIR abnormality involves the optic radiation and reaches the arcuate fasciculus; tractography defines the subcortical limit of resection (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 with IDH1 R132H IHC negative, ATRX retained and MGMT promoter methylated, with TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification and +7/-10
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by maximal safe resection of the left temporal lesion, or stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, ATRX immunohistochemistry and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery is the first option for a resectable glioma and should be as extensive as safely possible (AIOM Q1; EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis and the molecular results that select treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Aspirin with dexamethasone raises gastrointestinal bleeding risk and aspirin is stopped before craniotomy; levetiracetam does not interact with dexamethasone

action_criteria.rationale: He takes aspirin, amlodipine and rosuvastatin and is on dexamethasone, with levetiracetam to start; enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs are avoided.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture: 5 mm midline shift from a large temporal mass carries a risk of herniation
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not continue aspirin perioperatively without neurosurgical clearance given bleeding risk at craniotomy
Do not use enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital): they accelerate dexamethasone metabolism and interact with many anticancer drugs
required_recommendations: Obtain MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol) before any invasive procedure

Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the left temporal lesion with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography; awake language mapping is limited by the current comprehension and naming deficits, so the approach (awake mapping, asleep resection with subcortical monitoring, or biopsy) is decided after neurosurgical and neuropsychological assessment.

Continue dexamethasone, started on admission, for symptomatic vasogenic oedema at the lowest effective dose (for example 4 mg every 6 to 8 hours while mass effect is marked), with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery.

Start antiseizure treatment with levetiracetam for the documented 30-second episode of speech arrest with preserved awareness, a focal aware seizure; this is treatment of tumour-related epilepsy, not prophylaxis. Avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), which lower dexamethasone and chemotherapy exposure.
Obtain pre-operative labs (CBC, BMP, coagulation, type & screen) and discontinue aspirin at least 7-10 days before craniotomy

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, at age 64 with KPS 70, radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp 2005; EANO 2021), from which the MGMT-methylated tumour is expected to benefit most.

differential.key_features: Former smoker; no known primary malignancy; staging CT negative; infiltrative edema along white matter tracts favours a primary glioma, and tissue is glial

Immunocompetent patient; PCNSL typically presents as a homogeneously enhancing periventricular or deep gray matter mass with diffuse central DWI restriction; ring enhancement with central necrosis and elevated rCBV argue against lymphoma; tissue shows a GFAP-positive glioma

Mildly elevated CRP and ESR could suggest infection, but absent fever, normal WBC, restricted diffusion at the enhancing rim (not centrally as in pyogenic pus), and markedly elevated rCBV are inconsistent with pyogenic abscess

Age, sex, absence of prior demyelinating events, thick closed ring enhancement rather than open-ring, central necrosis, and markedly elevated rCBV and Cho/NAA all argue strongly against tumefactive MS

Progressive three-week course with worsening mass effect, thick irregular ring enhancement, and markedly elevated rCBV are incompatible with infarction; MRI restricted diffusion is at the tumor rim rather than vascular territory distribution

key_clinical_evidence: Three weeks of progressive aphasia (word-finding pauses, paraphasias, impaired comprehension and repetition) with morning headaches and a right superior quadrantanopia in a 64-year-old man localise to the left temporal lobe and require urgent contrast-enhanced MRI

MRI demonstrating a large left temporal ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis, restricted diffusion at the rim, perilesional FLAIR edema involving the optic radiation, and mild midline shift is characteristic of high-grade glioma; the optic radiation FLAIR signal explains the right superior quadrantanopia

Mildly elevated ESR (42 mm/hr) and CRP (7.8 mg/L) may prompt consideration of an infectious or inflammatory etiology (abscess, tumefactive MS), but no fever, no leukocytosis, thick irregular ring enhancement with necrosis, and markedly elevated rCBV are inconsistent with abscess or demyelination
Perfusion MRI (rCBV ratio 4.3) and MR spectroscopy (Cho/Cr 4.0, NAA/Cr 0.3, lipid-lactate peaks) support a high-grade neoplasm and target tissue sampling

The tumour lies in dominant language cortex: functional MRI places Wernicke area 4 mm from the margin and DTI shows a partly infiltrated arcuate fasciculus; because comprehension and naming are already impaired, awake language mapping may not be feasible and the surgical approach is decided after neurosurgical and neuropsychological assessment

Tissue, by maximal safe resection where feasible, establishes glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 (IDH1 R132H negative, ATRX retained, MGMT methylated, TERT mutation, EGFR amplification, +7/-10); imaging alone cannot distinguish it from other high-grade neoplasms

At 64 with KPS 70, glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, is treated after maximal safe resection with radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions and concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp 2005; EANO 2021); MGMT promoter methylation predicts greater benefit from temozolomide
The witnessed 30-second speech arrest with preserved awareness is a focal aware seizure and is treated with levetiracetam; this is treatment, not prophylaxis

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild nonspecific elevation of acute-phase reactants can occur in patients with large necrotic brain tumors due to tumor-induced systemic inflammation; the absence of fever, normal WBC, and the MRI features (thick irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, restricted diffusion at the rim, markedly elevated rCBV) are incompatible with infectious or demyelinating etiologies and establish high-grade neoplasm as the overwhelmingly likely diagnosis

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Darnell Washington is a 64-year-old right-handed African American man and retired high school history teacher who presents to the neurology inpatient service with a three-week history of progressive language dysfunction. His wife first noticed that he was pausing more during conversation approximately 21 days ago, initially attributing this to fatigue. Over the following week, the pauses became more frequent and he began substituting incorrect words, occasionally using completely unrelated words in sentences. He reported difficulty understanding his wife when she spoke more than a few words at a time, which he described as 'people are speaking too fast.' Over the past ten days, he has developed worsening headaches, predominantly left-sided and temporal in location, worst in the morning and partially responsive to acetaminophen. His wife reports that he has seemed more forgetful over the past week, missing two tutoring appointments and repeatedly asking the same questions within short intervals. Two days prior to admission, he had a 30-second episode of complete speech arrest with preservation of consciousness, witnessed by his wife, after which he reported a brief throbbing headache. He also reports intermittent blurring in the upper right portion of his visual field, which his wife describes as him bumping into objects on his right side. He has had one episode of nausea without vomiting, occurring in the morning three days ago. He denies any prior episodes of speech difficulty, prior seizures, head trauma, fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss. He has no history of malignancy and no recent travel outside the continental United States. A non-contrast head CT obtained at an urgent care visit yesterday showed a left temporal mass with surrounding hypodensity consistent with edema and approximately 5 mm of rightward midline shift, and he was referred urgently to neurology. He was admitted for further evaluation and was started on dexamethasone for symptom management.

neurological_exam.additional: No meningismus. No papilledema. No witnessed seizure events during the current evaluation. Patient had one episode of speech arrest lasting approximately 30 seconds two days prior to admission, witnessed by his wife, without loss of consciousness or tonic-clonic activity.

Hearing grossly intact to finger rub bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person and place; mildly disoriented to date. Comprehension impaired for multi-step commands; follows single-step commands inconsistently. Repetition markedly impaired. Naming severely impaired across categories. Reading aloud impaired. Writing not tested due to cooperation difficulties. Serial sevens not assessable. Recall 1/3 objects at 5 minutes with phonemic cuing. Judgment and insight partially preserved; patient is frustrated and aware of his language difficulty.

neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch and pinprick decreased in the right hand and forearm compared to the left. Proprioception intact at the great toes bilaterally. Vibration sense intact at the ankles bilaterally. Graphesthesia impaired in the right hand.
